sentences.text: This appeal is preferred by the claimants challenging the judgment and award dated 11.10.2019 passed by the Additional Small Causes Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru (for short 'the Tribunal') in MVC No.3940/2018.

entities.text: Additional Small Causes Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: This appeal is founded on the premise of inadequacy of compensation.
Hence, the appellants seek enhancement of compensation.
2. Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the tribunal.

Brief facts of the case are as under; That on 26.02.2018, Sri Ananda along with his friends namely, Sathish and Kirankumar and his brother- in-law Mahesh had gone to Hunsur to attend a marriage function by two motor cycle.

While returning at Nelamane near Arakalgud by pulsar motor cycle bearing No.KA-13- EL-6354, Hunsur-Periyapattana main road, they reached near lake of Nagamangala village at 4.30 p.m., at that time, a KSRTC bus bearing No.KA-09-F-5229 came from Hunsur towards Periyapattana, driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and safety, dashed against the motor cycle of Ananda, who fell down and sustained grievous injuries to his head, consequently, succumbed to the injuries on the spot.

entities.text: Smt Shruthi C vs The Managing Director Ksrtc

sentences.text: It is stated that the deceased was shifted to Sri D.Devarajurs General Hospital, Hunsur for postmortem, where they spent Rs.50,000/- towards transportation of dead body, funeral and other expenses.

NC: 2024:KHC:1938 It is stated by the claimants that prior to the occurrence of accident, deceased Ananda was hale and healthy, aged about 33 years working as a car driver, he was earning more than Rs.30,000/- per month.

The claimants were solely dependent on the earnings of the deceased for the maintenance and livelihood and due to the sudden and an untimely demise due to the negligence of the driver of the bus, the claimants had sustained severe financial distress, mental shock, agony, pain, they lost their loved one and the earnings of the deceased.
Hence, the claimants filed the claim petition seeking compensation.

3.2 On service of notice, respondent-Corporation filed statement of objections, denied the averments made in the claim petition and pleaded that it was fault of the rider of the motor cycle,
due to which, the accident occurred and it was not due to the negligence of the driver of the bus.

Hence, sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
NC: 2024:KHC:1938 3.3
On the basis of pleadings, the tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.
3.4 In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, claimant No.1 got examined herself as PW.1 and another witness as PW.2 and got marked documents as Exs.P1 to P13.
On the other hand, respondent-Corporation examined one witness as RW.1 and did not mark any documents.

3.5 On the basis of material evidence, both oral and documentary and on hearing the submissions of learned counsel for both parties, the tribunal has awarded the compensation of Rs.13,66,000/- with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the deposit and also held respondent liable to pay the compensation amount to the claimants and directed to deposit the said amount within three months.
NC: 2024:KHC:1938 3.6 Being aggrieved by the meager compensation amount awarded by the tribunal, the claimants are before this Court seeking enhancement of compensation.

4. It is the vehement contention of the learned counsel for appellants-claimants that the tribunal has committed serious error in not assessing the correct income and has ignored the materials placed on record, with regard to the deceased being a driver.

He also contends that the tribunal has not awarded future prospects as contemplated in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs.
Pranay Sethi and others reported in (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680.

entities.text:
National Insurance Company Limited vs.
Pranay Sethi and others reported in (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, the tribunal has committed miscarriage of justice in awarding meager compensation.

It is also contended that the tribunal has not awarded suitable compensation towards consortium and hence, they are before this Court seeking enhancement of compensation.
NC: 2024:KHC:1938 Smt Shruthi C vs The Managing Director Ksrtc on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5373436/
3 5.

entities.text: 2024:KHC:1938 Smt Shruthi C vs The Managing Director Ksrtc
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for respondent- Corporation contends that the tribunal has awarded just and reasonable compensation on the basis of materials placed on record, as no proof of income was placed before the Court.

It is contended that the tribunal has taken correct notional income,
which does not call for interference and in all other heads, the tribunal has awarded reasonable compensation.
Therefore, on these grounds, he seeks dismiss the appeal.
6. Having heard learned counsel for appellants- claimants and learned counsel for respondent, it is not in dispute that the accident occurred on 26.02.2018.

Deceased was traveling on the motor cycle,
the driver of the bus dashed against the vehicle of the deceased from behind, due to which deceased fell down and died on the spot.

In order to substantiate these aspects, the claimants have produced the documents as Exs.P1 to P13, out of which, Exs.P1 to P7 are the police records and NC:
2024:KHC:1938 Exs.P8 to P13 are the records to show the age and proof of income of the deceased.

7. On careful consideration of the materials and the submission of learned counsel for both parties,
it is seen that the tribunal assessed the income of Rs.9,000/- per month, is on the lower side,
whereas, notional income chart of the Legal Services Authority prescribes the income of Rs.12,500/-
for the accident year 2018.
Accordingly, income is taken as Rs.12,500/-.
The age of the deceased was 33 years.

The tribunal has rightly applied the multiplier at '16' as contemplated in the case of Sarla Verma (Smt) and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121, which does not call for interference.

entities.text: Sarla Verma (Smt) and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I am an agreement with the learned counsel for appellants-claimants that the tribunal has failed to award future prospects, in view of deceased being aged 33 years, 40% would have to be added to the income as future prospects.
There are four dependents to the NC: 2024:KHC:1938 deceased, hence, 1/4th would have to be deducted towards personal and living expenses.

Hence, the income shall be taken as Rs.13,125/- (Rs.12,500/- + 40% -
1/4th).
Hence, loss of dependency would be Rs.25,20,000/- (Rs.13,125/- x 12 x 16) as against Rs.12,96,000/- awarded by the tribunal.
8. Towards loss of consortium and loss of love and affection, the tribunal has awarded totally Rs.90,000/-.

As there are four dependents, each would be entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/- as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs.
Pranay Sethi and others reported in (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680 followed by Magma General Insurance Co.Ltd. vs. Nanu Ram and others, reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130 and Sarla Verma (Smt) and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.

Therefore, under the head of loss of consortium, the claimants are entitled for - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:1938 Rs.1,60,000/- (Rs.40,000/- x 4) along with 10% escalation towards one block period, which would be Rs.1,76,000/- (Rs.1,60,000/- + 10%).
9.

The tribunal has awarded totally Rs.30,000/- under the head of loss of estate and transportation of dead body and funeral expenses, whereas, 10% escalation towards one block period is required to be granted, which would be Rs.33,000/- (Rs.30,000 + 10%) in all.
